sentences.text: Coram:Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad Hon'Ble

Mr. Justice Navneet
Kumar
For the Appellant : Mr. R.S.Mazumdar, Sr. Advocate Mr. Nishant Kumar Roy, Advocate For the Respondent : Mr. Pankaj Kumar, Public Prosecutor ------
Order No. 08/Dated 17th August, 2023 I.A. No.5174 of 2023

With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the instant interlocutory application has been heard which has been filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence dated 25.05.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO), Godda in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.35 of 2018 arising out of Mahagama P.S. Case No.67 of 2017, corresponding to G.R. Case No.757 of 2017, by which the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(1) of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years with fine of Rs.50,000/- for the offence under Section 376(1) of IPC and in default of payment of fine, has been further directed to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for one year.

2. Mr. R.S. Mazumdar, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, has submitted that it is a case where without coming to the conclusive proof about the age of the victim, conviction under Section 4 of the POCSO Act has been passed.

sentences.text:
It has been contended by referring to the provision of Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 wherein the process for determination of the age has been provided but it is evident from the impugned judgment that on the basis of the Admission Register the age of the victim has been assessed to be 17 years, 3 months and 3 days.
4.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It has further been submitted that since the age of the victim has not conclusively been proved as per the statutory command as provided under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and, as such, it is a case where the main ingredients either of Section 376 I.P.C. or Section 4 of the POCSO Act are not available since, it is evident from testimony of PW-7, more particularly paragraph 15 of the impugned judgment, as per the version of the Investigating Officer, the victim and the appellant used to talk with each other as was surfaced from the details of call record of the appellant and victim.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. The learned senior counsel, based upon the aforesaid premise, has submitted that it is a fit case where the prima facie case is made out for suspension of sentence.

6. While on the other hand, Mr. Pankaj Kumar, learned Public Prosecutor, has submitted on the strength of the affidavit in objection which has been filed in terms of the order dated 20.07.2023,
that it is incorrect in taking the ground that the age has not conclusively been proved to be 17 years,
3 months and 3 days, based upon the Admission Register which is on the basis of the statutory command as under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Since the learned trial court has come to the conclusive evidence of the age considering the victim to be a minor and in that view of the matter if the conviction is under Section 4 of the POCSO Act taking into consideration the testimony of the other witnesses, the same cannot be said to suffer from an error.
7.
The learned Public Prosecutor, on the basis of the aforesaid premise, has submitted that it is not a fit case for suspension of sentence.

8. We have heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the finding recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned judgment as also the lower court records which have been called for by this Court vide order dated 28.06.2023.
9.

It appears from the testimony as has been discussed by the learned trial court that the victim has been found to be the age of 17 years, 3 months and 3 days and, as such, the victim comes under the fold of the definition of Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act.

The learned trial court, considering the victim to be a child within the meaning of Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act and taking into consideration the aforesaid fact has found the substantial evidence against the appellant which led him to convict the appellant under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

10. The argument which has been advanced on behalf of the appellant that before passing the judgment of conviction under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, the requirement of law as per Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 to come to a conclusive evidence Suraj Kumar Boby vs The State Of Jharkhand on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91725405/
2 regarding the age of the victim and that is the sine qua non for passing the judgment of conviction under the POCSO Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. We are not in disagreement with such submission, since, procedure has been laid down for determination of the age of the victim before considering the ingredients of any offence as enshrined under the POCSO Act.

The said procedure has been laid down under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 wherefrom it is evident that the certificate of the Headmaster or matriculation certificate is the proof of date of birth and in absence thereof the victim is to be examined by the Medical Board for the purpose of the ossification test.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The age is to be determined based upon either of the documents as referred under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 but herein, it appears from the material available on record that the victim has been assessed on the basis of the admission register of the concerned school.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, argument as has been advanced on behalf of the appellant that there is no conclusive proof of the age and hence, the ingredient of Section 4 of POCSO Act is not available prima facie appears to be correct.
12. The other argument by referring the testimony of PW-7 has been made which has also been considered by this Court.

It is evident from the testimony of PW-7, i.e., the Investigating Officer,
who has deposed as under paragraph 15 thereof that both the appellant and the victim were in the talking term.
Such fact was surfaced on the basis of the CDR of the cellphone used by them.

13. Since the application herein is for suspension of sentence, wherein at the stage of suspension of sentence the appellate court is to look into the prima facie case, if made in favour of the appellant,
then sentence is to be suspended.
14. This Court, on the basis of the aforesaid discussion, is of the view that the appellant is able to make out prima facie case for suspension of sentence.
15. Accordingly, the sentence is hereby suspended.
16. I.A. No.5174 of 2023 stands allowed.

17. In consequence thereof, the appellant named above, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned learned Special Judge (POCSO), Godda in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.35 of 2018 arising out of Mahagama P.S. Case No.67 of 2017, corresponding to G.R. Case No.757 of 2017.
18.
It requires to refer herein that whatever observation has been made hereinabove will not prejudice the case of the appellants on merit since the appeal is lying pending for its consideration.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Birendra/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:

The age is to be determined based upon either of the documents as referred under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 but herein, it appears from the material available on record that the victim has been assessed on the basis of the admission register of the concerned school.
